requirements.title: Stable Baseline Identity And Version
requirements.requirement: Every governed baseline has stable logical identity and an immutable behavior-relevant version. Material changes create a new version. External services that cannot guarantee immutable backend behavior preserve provider identity, advertised revision, timestamp, configuration, captured outputs, and the resulting reproducibility limitation rather than claiming exact pinning.

requirements.title: Pre-Protected Baseline Binding Freeze
requirements.requirement: Before protected outcomes are inspected, bind baseline identity, version, role, selection rule, comparison configuration, and resource-comparison regime. Subsequent changes inherit Task 7 freshness, repeated-peeking, disclosure, lineage, and invalidation semantics and create successor evidence rather than rewriting the earlier comparison.

requirements.title: Strongest Applicable Comparator Selection
requirements.requirement: Where a strongest applicable comparator is required, predeclare the eligible comparator class, applicability criteria, matching constraints, selection evidence, selection rule, and tie policy. Preserve materially considered comparators and exclusion reasons. Protected outcomes may not determine eligibility, exclusion, or selection. 'Strongest applicable' is bounded to the governed eligible matched set and is not a claim of global optimality.

requirements.title: Diagnostic Anchors And Claim-Bearing Comparators
requirements.requirement: Distinguish diagnostic anchors, ordinary claim-bearing matched comparators, and strongest-applicable comparators. A favorable result against a simple anchor cannot satisfy or obscure failure against a stronger comparator required by the hypothesis. Any anchor used must still be credibly implemented for its declared diagnostic role.

requirements.title: Information And Opportunity Parity
requirements.requirement: Candidate and baseline receive materially comparable task information, data access, protected-outcome restrictions, tools, permissions, external-service opportunity, and interaction opportunity unless a difference is the predeclared treatment under evaluation.

requirements.title: Evaluation Parity
requirements.requirement: Candidate and baseline are evaluated against the same applicable evaluation units, split version, evaluator contract, outcome semantics, and hard constraints unless a scientifically justified difference is declared before protected inspection.

requirements.title: Declared Treatment And Legitimate Asymmetry
requirements.requirement: Fairness does not require identical internal algorithms. Any material candidate-versus-baseline asymmetry must be classified as treatment, required method-specific operation, resource-regime difference, or comparison defect. Undeclared asymmetry blocks a claim whose interpretation depends on matching.

requirements.title: Tuning And Model-Selection Governance
requirements.requirement: Predeclare candidate and baseline tuning spaces, development and validation evidence, search procedure, stopping rule, selection criterion, and protected-data prohibition. Tuning opportunity may not be intentionally asymmetric to weaken the comparator. Task 9 owns concrete search and engineering-effort accounting.

requirements.title: Exact Comparison Provenance
requirements.requirement: Preserve material candidate, baseline, target, model/provider, prompt/policy, scaffold, inference, tool, permission, evaluator, environment, split, data, source revision, dependency, seed, timestamp, and external-service provenance needed to interpret the comparison. Unknown provider or evaluator revision state is recorded as unknown rather than invented.

requirements.title: Reproducible Comparison Manifest
requirements.requirement: Each consequential comparison has a versioned experiment manifest capable of reconstructing or faithfully replaying the comparison to the extent permitted by the underlying systems, using integrity-checked artifacts where practical. Nondeterministic or externally controlled dependencies carry explicit reproducibility limitations.

requirements.title: Stochastic Replication And Stopping Governance
requirements.requirement: When material stochasticity exists, predeclare replication unit, attempt count or stopping rule, controllable seed/sampling policy, aggregation, uncertainty method, and major variation sources. Outcome-driven optional stopping is prohibited for protected scientific conclusions unless governed in advance. Repeated runs do not manufacture independent Task 7 evaluation units.

requirements.title: Effect Size And Statistical Uncertainty
requirements.requirement: Scientific superiority comparisons report the predeclared effect measure and applicable uncertainty under a model consistent with the evaluation-unit and dependency design. Valid paired structure is preserved when applicable. Statistical significance cannot replace material effect size or weaken Task 6 thresholds.

requirements.title: Primary Measures And Selective-Reporting Control
requirements.requirement: Predeclare primary claim-bearing measures, secondary or diagnostic measures, aggregation rules, and any scientifically material multiplicity or selective-reporting policy before protected inspection. Task 8 must not invent corrections that override Task 6 hypothesis semantics.

requirements.title: Hard Constraints Cannot Be Averaged Away
requirements.requirement: Applicable hard constraints remain separately evaluated from aggregated performance. A favorable mean, composite, or secondary metric cannot convert a critical-invariant, authorization, protected-data, retention, locality, rollback, or other governed hard-constraint violation into PASS.

requirements.title: Benchmark Construct, Portfolio, Coverage, And Claim Scope
requirements.requirement: Document benchmark construct, environment family, claim scope, coverage, omissions, difficulty relevance, dependency structure, and expected relation to intended real-world behavior. When portfolio, subset, task-sampling, or difficulty selection can change the conclusion, freeze those rules before protected outcomes.

requirements.title: Contamination And Exposure Provenance
requirements.requirement: Represent known, suspected, unknown, and ruled-out contamination or exposure relationships that materially affect interpretation. Dynamic generation does not imply cleanliness; dynamic benchmarks must still satisfy construct, difficulty, provenance, leakage, evaluator, and reproducibility requirements. Task 7 remains the authority for protected-data contamination semantics.

requirements.title: Evaluator Identity, Validity, Bias, And Artifact Control
requirements.requirement: A claim-bearing evaluator has explicit identity, version, configuration, construct, scoring procedure, and known limitations. Where material, qualification addresses order or position effects, formatting or verbosity bias, answer-parsing artifacts, evaluator-model bias, calibration, and independent or alternative cross-checks. An evaluator defect can invalidate the affected comparison and must not be attributed to candidate or baseline capability.

requirements.title: E1 Outcome And Observable Trajectory Evidence
requirements.requirement: When execution behavior affects interpretation, preserve outcome separately from observable trajectory evidence such as actions, tool calls, environment transitions, retries, refusals, termination, harness failures, and evaluator-visible policy events. Claim-affecting trajectory categories and classification rules are predeclared; ambiguous cases remain UNKNOWN rather than being forced into a favorable explanation. Private model chain-of-thought is neither required nor requested.

requirements.title: N-H2 Transfer Comparator Isolation
requirements.requirement: N-H2 comparisons distinguish learned cross-family transfer from target-starting references, fixed or non-learned methods, shared infrastructure, retrieval, target-specific prompts, onboarding, manual target engineering, and other information transfer. Source-side learned advantage remains separately demonstrable, and protected target outcomes cannot tune the transferred mechanism.

requirements.title: A-H1 Adaptation Comparator Set
requirements.requirement: A-H1 binds the frozen pre-adaptation state, no-adaptation reference, strongest applicable matched adaptation baseline, and scientifically necessary conventional update comparator where valid. Adaptation comparator eligibility, tuning, and exclusion provenance follow the same strongest-applicable safeguards as other claim-bearing baselines.

requirements.title: A-H2 Retention, Locality, And Verified Rollback
requirements.requirement: A-H2 separately preserves pre/post adaptation prior capability, locality, critical invariants where applicable, rollback execution, relevant restored state, and protected post-rollback behavior. Successful rollback invocation alone is insufficient. Target improvement cannot substitute for retention, locality, or rollback evidence.

requirements.title: Resource-Comparison Regime And Task 9 Boundary
requirements.requirement: Before protected inspection, freeze the applicable semantic resource regime, such as strictly matched, budget-capped, or unconstrained-but-jointly-reported, and identify materially relevant resource dimensions. Task 9 owns concrete definitions, measurement procedures, and observed token, API, compute, time, memory, storage, monetary, and human-effort values.

requirements.title: Baseline Supersession And Recomparison
requirements.requirement: Credible evidence of a materially relevant stronger comparator or a baseline defect triggers governed reassessment under the applicable BASELINE evidence consequence. Historical evidence remains preserved. Recomparison follows Task 7 freshness and lineage rules and never rewrites the earlier result.

requirements.title: Missing Comparator Blocks Or Narrows The Claim
requirements.requirement: When a required meaningful comparator cannot be implemented or reproduced, do not manufacture a weak substitute. The broader claim remains BLOCKED, INCONCLUSIVE, or otherwise truthfully dispositioned. Any narrower successor claim preserves the original evidence gap and cannot imply the blocked broader superiority claim.

requirements.title: Benchmark Evidence And Real-World Validity
requirements.requirement: Automated benchmark evidence supports only the represented claim scope. Additional simulation, red-team, user, field, shadow, replay, or other evaluation is triggered when the exact claim materially depends on open-ended operation, humans, long horizons, changing environments, workflow integration, production constraints, or safety-relevant behavior. Benchmark success is not production-readiness evidence by default.

requirements.title: Claim-Proportionate Independent Verification
requirements.requirement: Consequential comparisons are independently verifiable under Task 7. The verification plan declares relevant separation across code, evaluator, data access, transformations, aggregation, execution path, assumptions, or authority, and explicitly discloses shared dependencies. A nominal second script that reuses the same material defect does not establish independence.
